      - name: Probe every landing-page release link
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh --landing site/index.html
      - name: Probe the full required asset set
        env:
          GITHUB_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh --smoke "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

  # Advance the vpinned release marker to the freshly signed tag. PURE
  # RELEASE-ARTIFACT MANIPULATION — no commits, no pushes: pin_release.sh
  # re-verifies the target's signature itself (fail-closed), then uploads
  # the PINNED_VERSION asset to the standing `vpinned` release. Runs after
  # release-provenance so the signed SHA256SUMS it checks are already
  # published. The marker is only a pointer — installers verify the pointed
  # release's signature against the committed trust anchor, so a tampered
  # marker degrades to a DoS, never a bad binary.
  install-pin-bump:
    name: Advance vpinned marker
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: release-provenance
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # always(): when release-provenance FAILS (e.g. the binaries/signature
    # upload race), plain needs-gating leaves this job SKIPPED — and a
    # `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs, so the marker stays
    # stale forever (v1.0.483: publish+provenance flaked, the recovery rerun
    # went green, the marker never advanced). With always() the job RUNS
    # even after a failed provenance: pin_release.sh's own pre-move
    # provenance gate (check_install_pin.sh with FA_PIN_TARGET) fails the
    # job loudly instead of moving the marker — and a FAILED job IS part of
    # rerun --failed, so the recovery cascade reaches it.
    if: >-
      always() && github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Point the vpinned marker at ${{ github.ref_name }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/pin_release.sh "${{ github.ref_name }}"

  installer-smoke:
    name: Installer smoke
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    needs: [binaries, release-provenance]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Depends on binaries — no !cancelled() needed here: the skip chain is
    # already broken upstream by the binaries job's own guard (fa#456).
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: windows-latest
            kind: ps1
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            kind: sh
          - os: macos-latest
            kind: sh
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Run the one-line installer (PowerShell)
        if: matrix.kind == 'ps1'
        shell: pwsh
        run: ./site/install.ps1

      - name: Run the one-line installer (sh)
        if: matrix.kind == 'sh'
        shell: bash
        env:
          FA_INSTALL_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/fa-bin
        run: sh ./site/install.sh

      - name: Smoke the installed binary (Windows)

app-crap-gate:
    name: Flutter app CRAP ratchet
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes, flutter-tests]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no app/shared changes — flutter_app CRAP green-skipped (required context reported)"
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # only-down guard diffs thresholds against the base
          # gh-1477: blobless — historical blobs are never read.
          filter: blob:none
      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@2286a0c042b44434fe26d292bbce8d34f7ec662b # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - name: Pub cache (crap4dart)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}
          restore-keys: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}-
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: app-coverage-shard-*
          path: app-coverage-shards
      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          count=$(ls app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          if [ "$count" != "2" ]; then
            echo "::error::expected 2 app shard coverage reports, got $count"
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p flutter_app/coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info \
            app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info
      - name: Config guards — badge sync, exclude parity, only-down (AC1/E1/AC3)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          [ -n "$BASE_SHA" ] || BASE_SHA=HEAD~1
          python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down "$BASE_SHA"
      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: pin bumped 0.2.1 → >=0.9.5 for the gate framework.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 (analyzer 14.4 refresh).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 — Type-2 duplication gate.
          # crap4dart#3/#4 (2026-10-15): >=0.14.2 <0.15.0 — same bounded
          # pin as the core job; the broken_goldens detector fixes the
          # flipped configs rely on.
          # gh-1738: >=0.15.0 — same bounded pin as the core job; the
          # root config's similarity gate runs under this version.
          # coverage.run_tests: false in both configs — the merged shard
          # lcov above is the source; never re-run the suite here.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.15.0 <0.16.0"
          cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json > crap_report.json

name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref. Tag pushes: the
    # release gate (gh-2290).
    if: always() && ((github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) || (github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')))
    permissions:
      actions: write # gh workflow run — the tag-arm retrigger (gh-2290)
      contents: write
    steps:
      # gh-2290: the trip decision runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's
      # empty workspace has no scripts/ (the exit-127 class reddened the
      # dedupe pre-check on every arm, runs 38696670029/38696668627). The
      # checkout must be UNCONDITIONAL — the trip step runs on every arm
      # this job reaches, and a skipped checkout would empty the trip
      # output. Shallow: the script never reads history.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      # One jobs call in a SINGLE valid document (steps arrays are
      # embedded per job — no per-job follow-ups; `gh api --paginate`
      # concatenates page bodies and jq then reads only the first page —
      # verified against a 69-job run), then the extracted,
      # fixture-self-tested trip decision (scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh;
      # static-gate selftest: scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh). It trips
      # ONLY on the degraded-runner-kill signature — job conclusion
      # `failure` OR `cancelled` (the v1.0.745 kill landed as plain
      # `cancelled`) with at least one `cancelled` step or one UNCONCLUDED
      # (`null`) step (gh-2358: the v1.0.759 runner death froze the
      # mid-flight `flutter build ios` step — and every trailing step — at
      # `null`, invisible to a `cancelled`-step-only detector) and NO
      # `failed` step (a real test failure ends with a failed step,
      # including death after a real red — only the trailing steps freeze)
      # — and never on a real test failure, a skip, or a cancelled
      # never-started job.
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          gh run view "$RUN_ID" --repo "$REPO" --json jobs > watchdog-jobs.json
          bash scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh watchdog-jobs.json

      # ── PR arm: empty-commit push (unchanged remedy) ──────────────────
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true' && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger workflows — the retrigger must
          # re-fire CI, so it rides RELEASE_PAT (same as release/gardener).
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - name: Retrigger with an empty commit (fresh runner allocation)
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true' && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          HAS_PAT: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT != '' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$HAS_PAT" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PAT not configured — cannot retrigger"
            exit 0
          fi
          msg="ci: watchdog retrigger (degraded runner pool)"
          if [ "$(git log -1 --format=%s)" = "$msg" ]; then
            echo "head commit is already a watchdog retrigger — not looping"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git commit --allow-empty -m "$msg"
          git push origin HEAD:"${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}"

      # ── Tag arm (gh-2290): dispatch a fresh gate run on the tag ref ────
      # ONE retrigger max per tag (issue #194 loop-guard rule): a prior
      # workflow_dispatch run for this tag ref means the retrigger already
      # fired for this kill — never chain dispatches on a stuck pool.
      - name: Retrigger the tag gate (dispatch, fresh runner allocation)
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true' && github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          prior=$(gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch "$REF" \
            --event workflow_dispatch \
            --json databaseId --jq 'length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
          if [ "${prior:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::notice::a workflow_dispatch gate run already exists for $REF — not re-firing (one retrigger max per tag, gh-2290)"
            exit 0
          fi
          gh workflow run ci.yml --ref "$REF"

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)

#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays out — baselines are macOS-captured;
#                   the nightly build-release macOS row guards goldens on
#                   the pinned-font env, issue #1856 / #177 E5)

#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM

#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,

#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock

# script. On TERM/INT: if OUR child was never started and is not completed,
# cancel exactly that run (gh-172 containment — an orphaned queued run
# must not publish unattended when the pool revives) and fail naming the
# child, its last observed state, and the observed pool activity. A child
# that ever started — even if it is between jobs right now — is left
# alone: its own per-job server-side timeouts (#344) bound it.
#
# The handler marks "$dw_state/handler-ran" BEFORE its first gh call so the
# detached backstop (spawned at the correlation site below) can tell a
# handled death from a lost handler and never double-cancel. DW_TRAP_PARSE_
# DEATH=1 (test shim) installs a deliberately unparseable trap action,
# reproducing the bash-5.3 poisoned-parse death (exit 2, handler never runs)
# that lost the orphan-cancel on CI reds main b54f324c / PR #1958 6a49b3ec.
run_id=0
child_started=0
watch_started=0
last_state="(never polled)"
pool_note="no pool observation yet"
dw_state=""

orphan_cleanup() {
  local sig="$1" ec=143 now
  [ "$sig" = "INT" ] && ec=130
  if [ -n "$dw_state" ]; then
    : > "$dw_state/handler-ran" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  now=$(date +%s)
  if [ "$run_id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null \
      && [ "$child_started" -eq 0 ] \
      && [ "${last_state%%/*}" != "completed" ]; then
    echo "::error::leg terminated by $sig after $((now - watch_started))s — child $workflow run $run_id NEVER STARTED (last observed: $last_state; $pool_note); cancelling this orphaned child only (gh-1903 orphan-cancel) — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
    gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
      || echo "::warning::orphan cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)" >&2
  else
    echo "::error::leg terminated by $sig after $((now - watch_started))s — child $workflow run $run_id (started: $([ "$child_started" -eq 1 ] && echo yes || echo no); last observed: $last_state; $pool_note); nothing to cancel (gh-1903: never-started children only)" >&2
  fi
  exit "$ec"
}
if [ "${DW_TRAP_PARSE_DEATH:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  # Test shim: the action string the bash-5.3 poisoned parser dies on
  # (unbalanced `(` — parser_error → exit 2, orphan_cleanup never runs).
  trap 'orphan_cleanup TERM ( ' TERM
  trap 'orphan_cleanup INT ( ' INT
else
  trap 'orphan_cleanup TERM' TERM
  trap 'orphan_cleanup INT' INT
fi

dispatch
epoch=$(date +%s)
if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then

{"body":"Closes #2381
### Root Cause
- v1.0.766's PTY shard 2/3 died from a three-layer chain: the vm-service loopback WS died mid-coverage-gather (the #2331 load class); the test_core engine's run loop threw with its queue still pending (3 tests in flight, 10 suites never loaded — proven by the shard's own reporter: allSuites 26, 16 suite events, testStart 101 vs testDone 98); the abandoned suites' live pty2 children blocked the VM exit handshake (`Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode`, ×2348) until the 40-minute kill concluded the job `cancelled` → Quality gate red → no signed SHA256SUMS → `pin_release.sh` refused (`E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING`) → "Advance vpinned marker" red.
- The watchdog retrigger healed the wedge but red'd `Hostile ambient env`: `agent_cli_waiting_integration_test.dart` AC1 (#2260) reads `running.json` right after `pumpEventQueue()`, but the settle-side manifest removal is an unawaited file-IO chain — under load the assertion observed the pre-removal manifest (same SHA green in the original run).

### Fix
- `scripts/load_drop_retry.sh`: the sharded legs' wrapper now SIGKILLs a wedged runner on sustained `Attempt:N waiting for isolate` console spam (counted over the attempt's own fresh console bytes; results are already in the file-reporter; coverage is per-suite incremental) instead of burning the shard budget, and heals the abandonment: unfinished-test suites + never-loaded invocation targets join the bounded rerun inventory (merged on top of #2379's bounded loop + drain backoff, which landed on main mid-leg) — real failures join the rerun and keep the shard red; a missing reporter never widens the inventory.
- `scripts/gate_failed_targets.py`: `--unfinished` (started tests with no `testDone` → their suite paths) and `--loaded` (suite-event paths) projections; the default failed-paths contract for `FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES` is unchanged (verified: run 45200064457's real shard artifact → `--unfinished` = the 3 in-flight suites, `--loaded` = 16).
- `test/cli/agent_cli_waiting_integration_test.dart` AC1: the manifest leave is now observed via a bounded load-tolerant wait (gh-2378 house shape) with a loud fail at the bound.

### Test Coverage
- `test/scripts/gate_failed_targets_test.dart`: 15 tests — unfinished/loaded projections incl. a fixture of the REAL abandonment log.
- `test/scripts/load_drop_retry_test.dart`: 18 tests — the #2379 bounded-loop contract (AC1-13, merged) + gh-2381 AC20-24 driving the real wrapper with stubbed runners: wedge spam → group-kill → exact abandoned-inventory rerun → heals; rerun-still-red stays loud; exit-70 unfinished and never-loaded both rerun; the --append baseline keeps a rerun from being insta-killed by attempt-1 spam (caught by the real-artifact verification).
- `test/cli/agent_cli_waiting_integration_test.dart`: 29 tests pass.
- Full `dart test --exclude-tags integration,browser-ext,llm` suite: 15006 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failed (exit 0).

### Notes
- No product-code changes — CI infra + one flaky test; the wrapper's fast path (green run, no transient signature) exits 0 with a single invocation, byte-identical behavior to before.
- The gh-2290 watchdog retrigger stays as the outer net; this fix turns the wedge class from a cancelled 40-minute burn into a minutes-scoped targeted rerun.
- The "Advance vpinned marker" refusal is by-design provenance gating; it recovers once the ref goes green.

The kill signature per watchdog_trip_check.sh: job conclusion `failure` OR `cancelled` with at least one `cancelled` step (or a null step) and NO `failed` step. app-crap-gate: conclusion `cancelled`, step 12 `cancelled`, no failed steps → signature matches. So yes, if the watchdog had scanned AFTER 01:26:56, it would have tripped and dispatched a fresh gate run on the tag.   # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh allocation. NEVER `gh run
  # rerun`: it reallocates into the same degraded pool. One retrigger max
  # per head commit / per tag (loop guards below).
  # gh-2290: this used to be pull_request-ONLY — but since gh-1537
  # retired the main-push CI run, v* tag pushes are the ONLY push arm
  # this workflow receives, i.e. the release gate had NO watchdog at all.
  # The v1.0.745 tag run 4424840840 hung a PTY shard on the pty2
  # blocking-waitpid wedge (`Attempt:N waiting for isolate
  # _waitForExitCode to check in`, vendor/pty2 VENDORED class), burned
  # its 40-minute budget and was concluded `cancelled` — the aggregate
  # gate reddened and ci-red-report filed the ticket with nothing to
  # self-heal it. The tag arm retriggers via a `gh workflow run ci.yml
  # --ref <tag>` dispatch (a fresh allocation; tags cannot take an
  # empty-commit push — moving a v* tag would re-fire the release flow —
  # and GITHUB_TOKEN MAY trigger workflow_dispatch, 2022-09-08
  # changelog). The dispatch arm runs the full gate on the tag's exact
  # tree: release-pending never blocks dispatch arms (gh-1551) and
  # release-dedupe is false for non-release events (gh-1625 AC3).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

content.thinking:
The watchdog comment says: "The timeout-minutes above are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min, flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283)."

So the repo convention: `timeout-minutes` ≈ 2x healthy duration. But for app-crap-gate, healthy duration is 5.5 min and timeout is 6 min — clearly NOT 2x. That's the bug: the job grew (checkout of a growing repo with fetch-depth: 0 is 4-4.5 min; plus setup + analyze + check ~1.5-2 min = 5.5-6+ min total) while its timeout stayed at 6.

The fix: raise app-crap-gate timeout-minutes to a proper 2x-baseline value → healthy 5.5 min → 2x ≈ 11-12 min. Similar jobs: `coverage-gate` at 2790? Let me map the line numbers: 2690 is app-crap-gate with timeout-minutes: 6 at line 2695. Line 2790: timeout-minutes: 12 — which job is that? Let me check the neighbors: what are lines 205 (timeout-minutes: 6) and 1860 (6)? Those might be other small jobs.

Also let me verify the watchdog_trip_check.sh script so I can reference it, and see whether adding app-crap-gate to the watchdog needs has any downside (watchdog waits longer; timeout-minutes: 5 on watchdog itself — app-crap-gate ends ~01:26:58, watchdog would start right after, fine within its 5-min budget).

One more check — the `needs:` list of watchdog vs app-crap-gate's `needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes, flutter-tests]`. Adding app-crap-gate to watchdog needs creates an implicit dependency: watchdog waits for app-crap-gate to settle (success/failure/skip). app-crap-gate itself depends on flutter-tests which is already in watchdog's needs. No cycles. Fine.

Also — should the trip detector also treat a JOB-LEVEL timeout (conclusion cancelled with a cancelled step) the same? It already does — that's the signature it looks for. The problem was purely the race (scan at 01:26:38, kill at 01:26:56).

Now — is there anything else that failed? The quality gate reported only "a leg is cancelled (app-crap-gate)". The run conclusion was "cancelled" because... hmm, actually let me double check: the run conclusion "cancelled" — when the quality-gate job FAILS and other jobs are cancelled/skipped... GitHub determines run conclusion; a run where some jobs were cancelled (by job-level timeout) and others failed usually concludes "failure". Interesting that it's "cancelled". Whatever — the ci-red-report leg filed the ticket; the failed jobs listed are Quality gate + Advance vpinned marker.

Wait, actually, let me look more carefully at whether app-crap-gate's timeout kill triggered a run-level cancellation cascade... The run conclusion is "cancelled" but jobs after continued (quality gate, vpinned, train guard, ci-red-report). In GHA, a run's conclusion becomes "cancelled" only via explicit cancellation or... actually there's another path: if a job times out, the job is cancelled, and when the run finishes, GitHub computes the run conclusion — with cancelled jobs and no failed... but here quality gate FAILED. Hmm, GitHub's run conclusion with mixed failure/cancel is normally "failure". 

Not important for the fix. Let me also sanity check the OTHER ci-red class: is the `Advance vpinned marker` failure purely downstream? Yes — pin_release.sh refused to move the marker because v1.0.768 never published SHA256SUMS (the release train stops when the gate is red). It recovers when the ref goes green (the tag arm re-run via watchdog dispatch, or manual). So the fix is entirely: prevent the app-crap-gate timeout kill + close the watchdog race.

Let me now also look at scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh quickly, and confirm the watchdog needs edit point. Then check how "healthy duration" is documented for app-crap-gate anywhere (e.g., shard-rebalance.yml handles durations for shards).

Also: per the workflow, for a tag push the release train: quality gate red → release legs skipped → tag stays unsigned → no release published. The install-pin-bump job with always() runs and fails the provenance gate loudly (by design). Fine.

Next: check git repo state, then make the fix:

1. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` app-crap-gate: `timeout-minutes: 6` → `12`, with a comment citing the measured durations and gh-2389 (ticket key). Actually what's the convention for referencing? Comments reference issues like `gh-2389` and `#2383`. The ticket is gh-2389.

2. watchdog `needs`: add `app-crap-gate` — with the existing comment updated to explain why (the v1.0.768 incident: the scan raced the 6-minute kill; gh-2389). The comment currently says: "pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963; gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them."

I'd add app-crap-gate there and mention gh-2389: "gh-2389: app-crap-gate rides along too — v1.0.768's 6-minute kill landed 18s AFTER the scan completed (needs didn't include it), so the one-shot retrigger never fired".

Now, wait — I should think about whether raising the timeout is really the complete fix, or whether there's something deeper: the checkout taking 4-4.5 min with fetch-depth: 0 + filter: blob:none. Other jobs use fetch-depth: 0 too? The `guards` job (CRAP + duplication, core) — 3m21s total in this run, with checkout... let me compare what checkout the guards job does — if guards uses a shallower checkout, maybe app-crap-gate's only-down guard doesn't actually need full history? `check_crap_guards.py --only-down "$BASE_SHA"` diffs thresholds against BASE_SHA = HEAD~1 for tag pushes (github.event.pull_request.base.sha empty on tag push). So it only needs HEAD~1 — fetch-depth: 2 would do! Hmm, but the comment says "fetch-depth: 0 # only-down guard diffs thresholds against the base". BASE_SHA=HEAD~1 on tag runs. But wait — is that robust? For PRs it's pull_request.base.sha — full PR diff... but PRs to this repo are same-repo; base.sha is on main. fetch-depth: 0 needed for that. Changing checkout depth is a bigger behavioral change — NOT minimum. Don't touch it.

The measured data: green worst case 5m31s (checkout 3m53s). The 6-min timeout gives 29s margin — indefensible. 2x convention → 12. Raising to 12 aligns with the repo's stated 2x rule and covers checkout growing to ~9 min. That's the primary fix.

Let me also double-check the quality-gate job's leg classification: "Quality gate FAILED: a leg is cancelled (app-crap-gate)" — the gate treats cancelled as fail (by design, "skipped security = dodge = FAIL"). With the timeout raised, app-crap-gate completes and the gate goes green.

Now the TDD requirement: "Write a unit test that reproduces the bug. Run it — it MUST FAIL". For CI workflow changes, what unit tests exist? There's `scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh` (mentioned: "static-gate selftest: scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh") and tests for workflow validation? Let me check test/ for workflow-related tests — maybe there's a workflow lint/consistency test (e.g., test that watchdog needs covers long legs, or timeout sanity). Let me search.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Root cause**: `app-crap-gate` ("Flutter app CRAP ratchet", job 138144350678) was killed by **its own `timeout-minutes: 6`** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `app-crap-gate:`). The leg's real wall is ~5.5–6+ min: the `fetch-depth: 0` blobless checkout alone took 4m30s on this run (01:20:45→01:25:15, +37s vs the healthy run) and the final `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart check` step needs ~1m20s (healthy run: 1m16s) on top of ~30s of setup. Healthy v1.0.767 (run 45264822393, job 138018358954) finished in **5m31s — 29 s under the wall**; any ordinary runner variance trips the kill. The kill lands as job conclusion `cancelled` with the mid-flight step cancelled, and the aggregate gate treats a cancelled leg as red ("Quality gate FAILED: a leg is cancelled (app-crap-gate)").

**Secondary (self-heal gap)**: the watchdog — the designed remedy for exactly this degraded-runner kill class — missed it: `watchdog.needs` omits `app-crap-gate`, so the watchdog settled as soon as `coverage-gate` finished (01:26:14), ran its one-shot trip scan at 01:26:29–38 ("no degraded-runner-kill signature", `trip=false`) and exited **18 seconds before the kill landed** (01:26:56). Its own comment states the invariant: "They must be in `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot retrigger." Exactly that happened. Without the retrigger there was no fresh-allocation recovery inside the release flow.

**Cascade (downstream, by design)**: gate red → release train stops (`release-provenance`, `sign release checksums` skipped) → v1.0.768 publishes no SHA256SUMS → `Advance vpinned marker` (install-pin-bump, `always()`) fails its fail-closed pre-move provenance gate: `E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING` (404 on `releases/download/v1.0.768/SHA256SUMS`). This job recovers on its own once the ref goes green — it is a symptom, not a cause (same class as PR #2383's note).

**Impact**: every tag run in which this leg's checkout/analyze runs slightly slow reds the whole release: no publish, no signed SHA256SUMS, no vpinned marker advance, and a ci-red ticket per occurrence. The leg sat at 92% of its budget on the healthy run — the red was a matter of time.

arguments.content:
### Root Cause
- v1.0.768's release run (45302423375) red'd with zero product/test failures: `Flutter app CRAP ratchet` (`app-crap-gate`) was killed by its own job-level `timeout-minutes: 6` mid-`crap4dart check` with every completed step GREEN. The leg's real wall is ~5.5 min healthy (v1.0.767: 5m31s total — checkout `fetch-depth:0` blobless alone 3m53s + check step 1m16s = 29 s of margin); on v1.0.768 checkout took 4m30s (+37 s ordinary runner variance) and the job died at the 6-minute wall, concluding `cancelled` → `Quality gate FAILED: a leg is cancelled (app-crap-gate)` → release train stopped → no SHA256SUMS → `Advance vpinned marker` red on the by-design provenance gate (`E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING`).
- The designed self-heal missed too: `watchdog.needs` omitted `app-crap-gate`, so the one-shot degraded-runner scan completed at 01:26:38Z — 18 s BEFORE the kill landed (01:26:56Z) — `trip=false`, no fresh-allocation retrigger. The watchdog's own comment states exactly this failure mode; gh-2389 observed it.

### Fix
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `app-crap-gate`: `timeout-minutes` 6 → 12 (≈2× the measured healthy wall, the watchdog doctrine; matches the sibling 5-min `test-faui` shards; a real hang is still killed loudly).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `watchdog.needs`: + `app-crap-gate` — the scan now settles after the leg, so a future kill of it still gets the one-shot retrigger.
